<description>
Bitcoin Core signs Taproot inputs with all-zero BIP340 auxiliary data. BIP340 recommends fresh randomness there, as protection against fault injection and side-channel attacks. I made `CreateSchnorrSig` pass `GetRandHash()` instead.

In the unit tests, only `script_tests/bip341_keypath_test_vectors` depended on the zero value: the BIP341 vectors were made with zero auxiliary data. It now signs each input twice, checks that the two signatures differ and both verify, and still matches the vector signatures by calling `SignSchnorr` with zero auxiliary data. The new check fails on master for all 7 key path inputs. The signing-related functional tests pass unchanged. The `script_sign` fuzz target can now reach `GetRandHash()`, so it seeds the RNG like the other signing targets.

I chose `GetRandHash()` over `GetStrongRandBytes()`. Both draw from the same RNG, which is seeded with OS entropy at startup, so the output is unpredictable; `GetRandHash()` skips the OS call `GetStrongRandBytes()` makes on each draw. BIP340 says any non-repeating value increases protection against fault injection, and that no security property other than side-channel resistance depends on the quality of this randomness. In unit tests `GetRandHash()` follows the test seed, so the tests stay reproducible; `GetStrongRandBytes()` does not.

Signatures are no longer deterministic, and this PR adds no option to make them so: nothing needs one today. If reviewers want one, for example to reproduce external test vectors, I can add an optional auxiliary value to `SignOptions`.

Fixes #31883.

*Written with LLM, a computer and the Internet; the mistakes, as usual, are all mine.*
</description>

be2bc19726 sign: use fresh randomness as BIP340 auxiliary data

MutableTransactionSignatureCreator::CreateSchnorrSig passed all-zero
auxiliary data to SignSchnorr. BIP340 recommends fresh randomness there,
for protection against fault injection and side-channel attacks. Pass
GetRandHash() instead.

The BIP341 key path vectors were generated with zero auxiliary data, so
the test no longer compares the creator's signature byte for byte. It
now checks that two signatures differ and are both valid, and
reproduces the vector signature by calling SignSchnorr with zero
auxiliary data.

The script_sign fuzz target can now reach GetRandHash() through
SignTransaction, so it seeds the global RNG like the other signing
targets.
</commits>
